commit_message:
[19.2.x][FlightReply] Don't drop FormData entries in `decodeReplyFromBusboy`

Fixes a regression from #36425 where referenced `FormData` entries can
be dropped by `decodeReplyFromBusboy` when files are interleaved with
text fields in the payload.

`decodeReplyFromBusboy` queues text fields that arrive while a file is
being streamed and flushes them after the last file's `'end'`, working
around busboy emitting `'end'` deferred relative to subsequent `'field'`
events. With multiple files interleaved with text, this loses the
relative order of the affected text entries. The reorder was a
long-standing but invisible issue — entries came back in the wrong order
but were all present — until #36425 tightened how referenced FormData
entries are collected from the backing store to rely on them being
contiguous. With that assumption violated, referenced FormDatas can now
come back with some entries dropped. The pattern is most easily surfaced
through `useActionState` actions that return the subm

The testDefinitions/React.d.ts stub used by internal TypeScript tests
was last updated for the class-component era. It was missing type
declarations for all React hooks and every API introduced since React 16.

This PR brings the stub up to date so the React team can write internal

Changes are purely additive — no existing declarations were removed or

- useActionState() with no-payload and typed-payload overloads (React 19)
- useOptimistic() with pass-through and reducer overloads (React 19)

[Flight] Fix stranded row content under Node stream backpressure (#36516)

The Flight Server emits Text and TypedArray rows as two chunks: a header
that gives the row's id, type, and content length, followed by the
content itself. These two chunks were pushed into
`completedRegularChunks` (and `completedDebugChunks` in DEV) as separate
items, so when the destination signaled backpressure between them, the
flush would write the header and then break out before reaching the
content. The content chunk was left stranded at the head of the queue.
Async work running while the destination was paused appended new rows to
`completedImportChunks` / `completedHintChunks`, and the next drain
flushed those queues first — splicing the newly-arrived bytes into the
position the Flight Client expects to read as the original row's
content. From there the Flight Client read rows from the wrong byte
offsets and the model failed to deserialize.

commit_message:
Throw special error if rejected Promises are incorrectly instrumented (#36328)

When a rejected `Promise` is instrumented in userspace while setting the
rejection reason in the wrong field (e.g. `error` instead of `reason`),
React will throw undefined (because `usable.reason` doesn't exist). This
makes it incredibly hard to find the actual rejection reason.

React is now throwing a generic error if we couldn't find the rejection
reason. That will produce a callstack pointing into the problematic
Promise from where you can hopefully extract the real rejection reason
(alongside fixing the bad instrumentation).

We're doing this in prod since this is unlikely to surface in dev. We're
only doing runtime type-checking for the rejected case. That should be
hit rarely and therefore hopefully have negligible runtime impact.

[FlightReply] Don't drop FormData entries in `decodeReplyFromBusboy` (#36468)

Fixes a regression from #36425 where referenced `FormData` entries can
be dropped by `decodeReplyFromBusboy` when files are interleaved with
text fields in the payload.

`decodeReplyFromBusboy` queues text fields that arrive while a file is
being streamed and flushes them after the last file's `'end'`, working
around busboy emitting `'end'` deferred relative to subsequent `'field'`
events. With multiple files interleaved with text, this loses the
relative order of the affected text entries. The reorder was a
long-standing but invisible issue — entries came back in the wrong order
but were all present — until #36425 tightened how referenced FormData
entries are collected from the backing store to rely on them being
contiguous. With that assumption violated, referenced FormDatas can now
come back with some entries dropped. The pattern is most easily surfaced
through `useActionState` actions that return the sub

Codegen registers `_c` (the memo cache import) as a side effect whenever
a function compiles with memo slots. The registration persists on
`ProgramContext.imports` even if the function is later discarded (`'use
no forget'`, `'use no memo'`, lint mode, validation errors). If other
applied functions in the file compile to 0 memo slots, the stale `import
{ c as _c } from "react/compiler-runtime";` leaks into the output.

function uses memo slots. If `react/compiler-runtime` has no remaining
specifiers, drop the module entry too so we don't emit a bare `import

commit_message:
Fix WorktreeCreatedTaskDispatcher overfiring on restored sessions (#318241)

Introduce onDidStartSession event to distinguish sessions we just started from sessions that appear in the catalog (via cloud sync, refresh, etc).

Problem:
WorktreeCreatedTaskDispatcher listened to onDidChangeSessions and tried to filter on status=Untitled to identify newly started sessions. This was wrong because:
- Agent-host sessions are never Untitled when arriving via change events (skeleton gets setStatus(InProgress) before firing)
- onDidChangeSessions fires for any catalog change including cloud-synced/restored sessions from other devices
- This caused tasks to run for existing sessions on every sync, not just newly started ones

Solution:
- Add onDidStartSession: Event<ISession> to ISessionsManagementService
- Fire it from sendNewChatRequest after provider.sendRequest() resolves with committed session
- Rewrite WorktreeCreatedTaskDispatcher to listen ONLY to onDidStartSession instead of added/changed

Git - throttle initial repository.status() across repositories

Each repository.status() spawns ~10 git subprocesses. With many repos in a workspace, fan-out can saturate the extension host and trigger the IPC unresponsive watcher kill loop. Bound concurrency with a Limiter(5).

Fixes #318279

Fixes #318764

commit_message:
preserve marketplace name through managed_settings policy delivery

The managed_settings adapter previously flattened extraKnownMarketplaces
entries to bare "<owner>/<repo>" or "<url>" strings, losing the marketplace
name. That broke enabledPlugins matching because plugin IDs are keyed as
"<plugin>@<marketplace-name>" but our parsed reference's displayLabel was
derived from the URL/repo instead.

Changes:
- adapter now emits { name, source } objects preserving the full shape
- IPolicyData.extraKnownMarketplaces accepts string | object entries
- parseMarketplaceReferences gains object-handling, using name as displayLabel
- workspacePluginSettingsService shares the object parser
- policy schema relaxed to allow object items

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Bump deb amd64 libc6 floor to 2.15 for new @github/copilot runtime.node

The new @github/copilot 1.0.55-3 ships a Linux x64 runtime.node that
references GLIBC_2.15 (was GLIBC_2.14 in 1.0.49). dpkg-shlibdeps now
emits libc6 (>= 2.15) for amd64; update the reference list so the deb
prepare task no longer fails the build.

Only amd64 is affected: arm64 runtime.node GLIBC version set is
unchanged, and @github/copilot does not ship an armhf binary. The
overall libc6 floor for the package is still 2.28, so distro support
is unchanged.

have no `fromMarketplace` metadata, so they previously bypassed enterprise
policy. Derive their identity from the install-path bucket (matching the
convention used by `_resolveEnterprisePluginId`) so enabledPlugins gating
applies, and add a bucket-name heuristic for strict marketplaces.

commit_message:
Make Linux desktop sanity tests robust to mid-test failures

The Linux desktop sanity tests (deb/rpm/snap) ran cleanup unconditionally
after `testDesktopApp` without a try/finally, so when that step threw
(e.g. extension install flake tracked in microsoft/vscode-engineering#2877)
the uninstall step was skipped. Mocha then retried the test, the install
step hit `package code-insiders is already installed`, and the retry
masked the real failure with a misleading error
(microsoft/vscode-engineering#2878).

Fix:
- Wrap install/test/uninstall in try/finally so cleanup runs even when
  the test body throws.
- Make the uninstall helpers idempotent by detecting whether the package
  binary exists; this lets the finally block run safely even if install
  itself fails (and avoids double-uninstall on the happy path).
- Add a pre-install assertion to each install helper that fails fast
  with a clear diagnostic when the package is already present, so any
  leftover state from a prior killed run su

commit_message:
fix: guard updateCollapseContextKeys against stale focus during tree splice

During tree setChildren/splice operations, focus-change events fire
synchronously while nodes are being removed from the tree's internal map.
The updateCollapseContextKeys handler then calls tree.getNode(focus) on
an element that no longer exists, throwing TreeError.

Add a try-catch around getNode to gracefully handle this transient state.
The context keys will be updated again once the tree settles and fires
another focus event.

Fixes #318777

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

During tree setChildren/splice operations, focus-change events fire
synchronously while nodes are being removed from the tree's internal map.
The updateCollapseContextKeys handler then calls tree.getNode(focus) on
an element that no longer exists, throwing TreeError.

Add a try-catch around getNode to gracefully handle this transient state.
The context keys will be updated again once the tree settles and fires
another focus event.

Fixes #318777

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
policy: enforce ChatEnabledPlugins and strict-marketplace gates at discovery

Previously the enterprise-managed policy values were delivered into the
policy framework but not  a plugin already installed locallyenforced
(e.g. via the marketplace discovery path) would remain active even when
the policy excluded it or strict-marketplace mode rejected its source.

Adds policy enforcement on AgentPluginService.plugins, applied after
discovery dedup/sort and gated by two observables:

- ChatEnabledPlugins policy: when set, filters the surfaced plugin set
  to only those whose '<name>@<marketplace>' ID appears in the policy
  map with value true. Plugins without a marketplace provenance
  (filesystem entries from chat.pluginLocations) are unaffected.

- ChatStrictMarketplaces: when on, filters out plugins whose source
  marketplace is not trusted. Trust is sourced ONLY from
  chat.plugins.extraMarketplaces (the policy-only  user-setslot)
  entries in chat.plugins.marketplaces do NOT grant tru

commit_message:
policy: split managed marketplaces into dedicated policy-only setting

Adds chat.plugins.extraMarketplaces (ChatExtraMarketplaces policy,
included: false so it's hidden from the Settings UI). This receives the
'extraKnownMarketplaces' payload from the managed_settings API.

Restores chat.plugins.marketplaces to its pre-PR shape: no policy slot,
no inspect()-juggling required in consumers, no risk of accidentally
clobbering user data. Users write to chat.plugins.marketplaces; the
enterprise writes to chat.plugins.extraMarketplaces; the effective set
is the union.

Consumer simplifications:
- readConfiguredMarketplaces returns { userValues, extraValues,
   two getValue() reads, no inspect() needed.effectiveValues }
- Write-back is now just [...userValues, refValue] in all three sites.
- 'Manage Plugin Marketplaces' still surfaces the 'managed by enterprise
  policy' badge by checking ref membership in extraValues.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
policy: address PR review feedback

- Restore historical default for chat.plugins.marketplaces
  (['github/copilot-plugins', 'github/awesome-copilot#marketplace']) so
  existing users don't lose the two built-in marketplaces on update.
  Regenerate policyData.jsonc accordingly.

- Seed _managedSettingsFetchStatus = 'ok' on cache-hit so Policy
  Diagnostics reports the applied state after a process restart that
  warm-starts from cached policyData (instead of stuck at 'not yet
  fetched').

- Scope the <plugin>@<marketplace> ID-resolution rule to the enterprise
  ChatEnabledPlugins setting only. User-typed entries in
  chat.pluginLocations that happen to contain '@' are now treated as
  filesystem paths, as a user would expect, not silently rewritten to
  ~/.copilot/installed-plugins/<x>/<y>/. Split _resolvePluginPath into

When setting FFI state via `TypeId` require passing `TypeInfo` as well. Templated APIs are supposed to be used in statically linked binaries, and when different FFI handlers can be in separate object files we rely on opaque type ids and state, and always lookup them through FFI API.

commit_message:
[XLA:CPU] Strip HostOffloarding and memory pinning annotations on XLA:CPU

On CPU, device-to-host copy offloading is physically a no-op, but JAX still inserts annotate_device_placement custom calls. If un-resolved, they cause the SPMD partitioner to crash.

Instead of using the complex, TPU/GPU-centric HostOffloader pass (which has alias-analysis crashes on Torax workflow loop due to multiple callers), we implement a lightweight StripMemoryPlacementAnnotations pass that strips these annotations early in the pipeline (pre-SPMD partitioner). We must also update the PjRt CPU client to track requested_output_memory_kinds and avoid runtime location mismatches.

PR #42259: [xla:ffi] When setting opaque state require TypeInfo

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/42259

When setting FFI state via `TypeId` require passing `TypeInfo` as well. Templated APIs are supposed to be used in statically linked binaries, and when different FFI handlers can be in separate object files we rely on opaque type ids and state, and always lookup them through FFI API.

This is one more fix required for making "internal" FFI headers "safe" when linked as multiple object files. This is still not safe in general and not recommended, but this is an escape hatch that makes it work correctly when XLA and FFI handler compiled with the same toolchain.

Add F6E3M2FN and F6E2M3FN to xla::PrimitiveType.

This CL introduces first-class declarations for two 6-bit floating point formats:
- F6E3M2FN (3 exponent bits, 2 mantissa bits)
- F6E2M3FN (2 exponent bits, 3 mantissa bits)

These types conform to the OCP Microscaling Formats (MX) specification:
https://www.opencompute.org/documents/ocp-microscaling-formats-mx-v1-0-spec-final-pdf

The encoding parameters are as follows:

FP6 E3M2 (Exponent bias: 3)
- Max normal: +/-28.0
- Min normal: +/-0.25
- Max subnormal: +/-0.1875
- Min subnormal: +/-0.0625

FP6 E2M3 (Exponent bias: 1)
- Max normal: +/-7.5
- Min normal: +/-1.0
- Max subnormal: +/-0.875
- Min subnormal: +/-0.125

PiperOrigin-RevId: 916256455

Add F6E3M2FN and F6E2M3FN to xla::PrimitiveType.

This CL introduces first-class declarations for two 6-bit floating point formats:
- F6E3M2FN (3 exponent bits, 2 mantissa bits)
- F6E2M3FN (2 exponent bits, 3 mantissa bits)

These types conform to the OCP Microscaling Formats (MX) specification:
https://www.opencompute.org/documents/ocp-microscaling-formats-mx-v1-0-spec-final-pdf

The encoding parameters are as follows:

FP6 E3M2 (Exponent bias: 3)
- Max normal: +/-28.0
- Min normal: +/-0.25
- Max subnormal: +/-0.1875
- Min subnormal: +/-0.0625

FP6 E2M3 (Exponent bias: 1)
- Max normal: +/-7.5
- Min normal: +/-1.0
- Max subnormal: +/-0.875
- Min subnormal: +/-0.125

This change introduces a new hlo module option that is checked by buffer assignment to create multiple heaps with a fixed size limit. Each heap is called a page and all buffers inside of the heap will get a page_id_ element set indicating which page they are located in.

Add F6E3M2FN and F6E2M3FN to xla::PrimitiveType.

This CL introduces first-class declarations for two 6-bit floating point formats:
- F6E3M2FN (3 exponent bits, 2 mantissa bits)
- F6E2M3FN (2 exponent bits, 3 mantissa bits)

These types conform to the OCP Microscaling Formats (MX) specification:
https://www.opencompute.org/documents/ocp-microscaling-formats-mx-v1-0-spec-final-pdf

The encoding parameters are as follows:

FP6 E3M2 (Exponent bias: 3)
- Max normal: +/-28.0
- Min normal: +/-0.25
- Max subnormal: +/-0.1875
- Min subnormal: +/-0.0625

FP6 E2M3 (Exponent bias: 1)
- Max normal: +/-7.5
- Min normal: +/-1.0
- Max subnormal: +/-0.875
- Min subnormal: +/-0.125

Preserve host memory space when automatic layout assignment is used

This CL fixes two problems:

- If an HLO module's result is a tuple `(host_array, device_array)`, and `device_array` uses automatic layout assignment, `host_array`'s memory space will be erased, even if `host_array` does not use automatic layout assignment, causing a `CompileTimeHostOffloadOutputLocationMismatch` error later in host_offloader.cc.
- If an HLO module's parameters/results contain a host memory space array and use automatic layout assignment, `LayoutModeToXlaShape` in pjrt/utils.cc erases the memory space, also causing a `CompileTimeHostOffloadOutputLocationMismatch` error.

commit_message:
[dynamo] Skip wrap_inline for exec'd Python functions (#181531)

## Summary

`OptimizedModule.__call__` wraps the target callable in `external_utils.wrap_inline` whenever `inspect.getsourcefile(fn)` returns `None`. The intent (per the inline comment) is to interpose a Python frame around C-level callables (builtins, slot wrappers, methods of C objects) that Dynamo cannot otherwise trace.

commit_message:
[dynamo] Skip wrap_inline for exec'd Python functions (#181531)

## Summary

`OptimizedModule.__call__` wraps the target callable in `external_utils.wrap_inline` whenever `inspect.getsourcefile(fn)` returns `None`. The intent (per the inline comment) is to interpose a Python frame around C-level callables (builtins, slot wrappers, methods of C objects) that Dynamo cannot otherwise trace.

Python functions created via `exec` / `eval` also report no source file. Wrapping those in `wrap_inline` is harmful: every such function ends up running through the same `inner` code object inside `wrap_inline`, with the original function captured as a closure cell. After `recompile_limit` (default 8) distinct exec'd functions have been compiled, the cache for that single `inner` code object fills up and Dynamo emits the recompilation warning. Under `fullgraph=True` this becomes a hard `FailOnRecompileLimitHit`.

## Fix

Narrow the `filename is None` clause to also require that `fn` is not a `types.Fu

commit_message:
[profiler] Synchronize all active devices on profiler exit (#181238)

The profiler's __exit__ previously called synchronize() without a device
argument, which only waits on the current device (default: device 0).
On multi-GPU workloads, this causes long-running kernels on non-zero
devices to be missed in profiling results.
Fix by synchronizing all devices with an active CUDA context in both
profile.__exit__ and emit_nvtx.__exit__. For non-CUDA backends, sync
all devices via device_count() since there is no hasPrimaryContext
equivalent.

Fixes https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/181238

Each compiled region now gets its own FIFO storage in the SAC dispatch modes,
keyed by the InductorCompiledCallable's unique idx. Previously all
inductor_compiled_code calls shared one queue keyed by the HOP, so a region
skipped during recompute (cache hit) would cause the queue to return the
wrong entry. The key resolves through _resolve_inductor_callable so both
the eager (callable-arg) and FX-replay (int-arg) forms are covered.

The regression test reproduces the mismatch on CPU using a fake process
group, so it runs in standard dynamo test jobs without requiring CUDA.

Authored with Claude.

Fixes #175258

non-fake tensor is encountered and it turns out to be a view of a
`FunctionalTensor` whose inner storage is a `FakeTensor`, we recover the
underlying `FakeTens

commit_message:
Address reviewer feedback: relax dunder test, add wrapper docstring

The dunder mangling test used plain `assertNotIn`, which false-fired
under inductor_cpp_wrapper: that path emits a `call_<kernel>` helper,
and stitching `call_` onto a stripped kernel name like
`_dunder_add_kernel_0` yields `call__dunder_add_kernel_0`. The double
underscore there sits inside a C++ identifier and isn't subject to
Python class-based name mangling, but the substring check flagged it
anyway. Switch the positive and negative assertions to word-boundary
regex so only standalone identifiers count.

Also add a docstring to `define_user_defined_triton_kernel`: after the
5-line strip added by this PR, the function crosses the DOCSTRING_LINTER
size threshold.

Signed-off-by: Yufeng He <40085740+universeplayer@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Fix SAC FIFO mismatch for inductor_compiled_code HOP

Each compiled region now gets its own FIFO storage in the SAC dispatch modes,
keyed by the InductorCompiledCallable's unique idx. Previously all
inductor_compiled_code calls shared one queue keyed by the HOP, so a region
skipped during recompute (cache hit) would cause the queue to return the
wrong entry. The key resolves through _resolve_inductor_callable so both
the eager (callable-arg) and FX-replay (int-arg) forms are covered.

The regression test reproduces the mismatch on CPU using a fake process
group, so it runs in standard dynamo test jobs without requiring CUDA.

Authored with Claude.

Fixes #175258

commit_message:
Update on "Replace __args__ with typing.get_args() and TensorType.dims"


Addresses #169073. Two changes:

1. TensorType (torch/fx/tensor_type.py) was using __args__ and __origin__
   to mimic a typing generic, but it's actually a domain type representing
   tensor dimensions. Added a `dims` property and migrated all internal
   usages from `.__args__` to `.dims` (the backing `__args__` attribute
   is kept for backward compat). This removes the confusion about whether
   TensorType should be accessed via typing.get_args().

2. Replaced all remaining `.__args__` accesses on standard typing generics
   (Union, List, Tuple, etc.) with `typing.get_args()`, the recommended
   public API. Covers operator_schemas, graph codegen, dynamo variables,
   inductor fuzzer, datapipes typing, and several other modules.

Authored with Claude.

commit_message:
Add regression tests for host caching allocator stats accounting

Two regression tests in TestCuda for host_memory_stats() bookkeeping
issues that were resolved by PR #171662 ("Add configurable threshold to
avoid power-of-two rounding for large pinned memory allocations") via
the introduction of the maybe_cache_block helper that consolidated
free()'s no-events fast path and process_events_for_specific_size:

1. test_host_memory_stats_active_after_free_no_events

   Asserts active_bytes.current and active_requests.current return to 0
   after a plain pin-and-drop cycle. Without the fix, free()'s no-events
   fast path pushed the block back to the free list without decrementing
   the active bucket stats, so the counters grew monotonically on every
   cycle even though the memory was correctly recycled.

2. test_host_memory_stats_active_after_event_drain

   Asserts the same after a pin / non_blocking H2D / drop / empty_cache
   sequence, plus that active_bytes.freed and active_requests.

commit_message:
crypto: runtime-deprecate calling Hmac.digest() more than once

Emit a DEP0206 deprecation warning when Hmac.digest() is called on an
already-finalized instance. This behavior is inconsistent with
Hash.digest() which throws ERR_CRYPTO_HASH_FINALIZED.

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/62838
PR-URL: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/REPLACEME

stream: import markPromiseAsHandled directly in pipeTo

Import markPromiseAsHandled directly from internalBinding('util') in
readablestream.js rather than re-exporting it through
internal/webstreams/util, so the C++ boundary stays visible at the
call site.

Also drop the verbose inline comments describing the
markPromiseAsHandled vs setPromiseHandled choice; the rationale lives
in the PR description.

Signed-off-by: Matteo Collina <hello@matteocollina.com>

commit_message:
domain: port to AsyncLocalStorage

Port the domain module from createHook (async_hooks) to
AsyncLocalStorage using the AsyncContextFrame-based implementation.

Key changes:
- Use AsyncLocalStorage for domain context propagation instead of
  async_hooks.createHook()
- Lazy initialization that triggers AsyncContextFrame prototype swap
  on first domain use
- Use enterWith instead of ALS.run() so domain context is NOT
  automatically restored on exception - this matches the original
  domain.run() behavior where exit() only runs on success
- Add ERR_ASYNC_RESOURCE_DOMAIN_REMOVED error for AsyncResource.domain
- Update DEP0097 to End-of-Life status
- Remove tests that relied on the removed MakeCallback domain property

The domain module now uses the AsyncContextFrame version of
AsyncLocalStorage directly for proper context propagation across
async boundaries.

Signed-off-by: Matteo Collina <hello@matteocollina.com>

commit_message:
debugger: defer probe pause handling until startup

Keep the initial --inspect-brk pause held until probe breakpoints are

Auto merge of #155849 - bushrat011899:io_slice_in_core, r=nia-e

Move `IoSlice` and `IoSliceMut` to `core::io`





ACP: https://github.com/rust-lang/libs-team/issues/755
Tracking issue: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/154046
Related: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/152918
Related: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155625

## Description

Moves `std::io::IoSlice` and `std::io::IoSliceMut` into `core::io`. This is required for the `Read` and `Write` traits to be moved into `alloc` and/or `core`, as they contain stable methods which work with IO slices. Similar to rust-lang/rust#155574, this PR inlines the `std::sys` types required to create an ABI compatible type for the platforms where such compatibility is guaranteed.

Additionally, I've moved the relevant tests out of `std::io::tests` into `coretests::io::io_slice`.

---

## Notes

* This PR overlaps with rust-lang/rust#152918, but goes further than moving the IO slice types to `alloc` and inst

Auto merge of #157007 - Kobzol:reject-invalid-backend, r=jieyouxu

Reject invalid codegen backends on CI

The way we set codegen backends in CI jobs contained several bugs.

1) We didn't check if the specified codegen backend is valid. That can be useful in forks, but not on our CI, there it should be a loud error.
2) The codegen backends were specified with weird quoting that was (I think) producing invalid backends.
3) The specified backends in `RUST_CONFIGURE_ARGS` were being overridden due to `run.sh` setting codegen backends based on the `CODEGEN_BACKENDS` environment variable (see https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/156989).

This PR should fix all of these.

After doing some CI runs on this PR, I realized that setting `CODEGEN_BACKENDS` from within the Dockerfile doesn't work, because we use `docker run --env CODEGEN_BACKENDS`, and that will unset the inner env even if the same env is not actually configured in the environment from where `docker run` is executed (sigh

coverage: Build the expansion tree around `SyntaxContext`

The expansion tree was previously built around `ExpnId`, which was subtly
incorrect in cases where multiple distinct syntax contexts share the same
`outer_expn` ID. This can occur in the presence of nested macro expansions.

This change turns out to be fairly straightforward, because in all cases we
were obtaining `ExpnId` from `span.ctxt().outer_expn()` anyway, so we can just
remove the call to `.outer_expn()` and use the context instead.

As a result of this change, `context-mismatch-issue-147339.rs` no longer
triggers a context mismatch in `extract_refined_covspans`.

commit_message:
Replace `Box<dyn TraitEngine>` with an enum.

`ObligationCtxt` contains a `Box<dyn TraitEngine>` that lets it switch
between trait solvers. Unfortunately, many short-lived `ObligationCtxt`s
are created and the allocation cost is non-trivial.

This commit introduces an enum `DualFulfillmentCtxt` that can hold an
old or new solver context, avoiding the need for the `Box` and making
things a bit faster.

commit_message:
std: cache `mach_timebase_info` on Apple

`mach_timebase_info` returns boot-time constants that never change for the
lifetime of the process. The current code path on every Apple target invokes
it on every call to `Instant::into_mach_absolute_time_ceil`, which is on the
hot path of `std::thread::sleep_until`.

A cache for exactly this value existed in the original implementation
(rust-lang/rust PR 77727, 2020). It was removed in the `clock_gettime`
migration (PR 116238, 2023) when `mach_timebase_info` stopped being used by
`Instant::now`. The trap was re-introduced uncached when `sleep_until` was
implemented for Apple (PR 151004, 2026).

Restore the cache using `OnceLock<(u32, u32)>` in a private helper, scoped
to the existing `#[cfg(target_vendor = "apple")]` gate. No API change, no
behavior change.

Auto merge of #156861 - Dnreikronos:fix/strict-provenance-macro-suggestions, r=mu001999

Suppress garbled suggestions from strict provenance lints in macros

The strict provenance lints (`lossy_provenance_casts`, `fuzzy_provenance_casts`) build suggestions using span arithmetic (`shrink_to_lo()`, `shrink_to_hi()`, `.to()`). When the cast sits inside a macro, those span operations produce broken output like `$e as ).addr()` because the spans don't map cleanly back to source text.

The fix wraps suggestion fields in `Option` and checks `can_be_used_for_suggestions()` before constructing them. The lint itself still fires, you just don't get the garbled suggestion. Same approach already used in `op.rs` and `static_mut_refs.rs` in this crate.

### What changed

- `errors.rs`: `sugg` fields in `LossyProvenanceInt2Ptr` and `LossyProvenancePtr2Int` are now `Option<...>`
- `cast.rs`: suggestion construction in both `lossy_provenance_ptr2int_lint` and `fuzzy_provenance_int2ptr_lint` is guarded b

commit_message:
ref_prop: do not collapse a mutable reborrow onto a multi-borrowed place

Fixes #132898.

ReferencePropagation set `targets[_3] = Pointer(_1.0, true)` for a mutable
reference `_3 = &mut _1.0`, so the Replacer would rewrite every `*_3` to `_1.0`
— including inside the reborrow `_2 = &raw mut (*_3)`, yielding
`_2 = &raw mut _1.0`. That shortens `_2`'s provenance from `_1 → _3 → _2` to
`_1 → _2`, which races an independent borrow of the root local (e.g. the
2-phase `&mut _1` for a method call), and the pass introduced Stacked Borrows
UB into code that was sound without the optimisation.

commit_message:
Wrap multi-bound `impl`/`dyn` after prefix type constructors

`&impl A + B`, `&mut impl A + B`, `*const impl A + B`,
`*mut impl A + B`, `&dyn A + B` and similar shapes parse as the
ambiguous `(&impl A) + B` and are rejected by the parser, so
diagnostics that surface them produce non-compilable Rust.
`refining_impl_trait` machine-applicable suggestions are the
user-visible failure.

In the `ty::Ref` and `ty::RawPtr` arms of `pretty_print_type`, wrap
the inner type in parens when it would print with `+`-joined bounds.
For `&mut`, emit the mutability prefix before the parens so the
output is `&mut (impl A + B)`, not the ill-formed
`&(mut impl A + B)`. `ty::Dynamic` already self-wraps under an
explicit region, so that case is skipped. `opaque_has_multiple_bounds`
mirrors `pretty_print_opaque_impl_type`'s sizedness handling, so
`?Sized` and the synthetic `Sized` suffix are counted correctly.

`LegacySymbolMangler` and `TypeNamePrinter` override
`add_disambiguating_parens_in_prefix_position`

Clear stale MemoryQoS cgroup values at kubelet startup

When MemoryQoS is disabled after being previously enabled, stale
memory.min and memory.low values persist on QoS-class cgroups because
systemd re-applies stored properties on every SetUnitProperties call.

Fix this by including memory.min=0 and memory.low=0 in the existing
startup dbus calls (enforceNodeAllocatableCgroups for the root cgroup,
qosContainerManager.Start for the burstable cgroup). This overwrites
systemd's stored stale values so subsequent realizations re-apply 0.

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/138436

commit_message:
scheduler/podtopologyspread: fix minMatchNum deflation caused by terminating pods in unreachable zones

Fixes #116629

The scheduler incorrectly excludes terminating pods when computing the global
minimum topology count (minMatchNum). When the terminating pod resides in a
zone that is unreachable for the incoming pod, this exclusion deflates the
minimum to zero and inflates skew for all other zones, causing a scheduling
deadlock.

This patch introduces a two-counter approach:

- existing counter (excludes terminating pods) continues to drive
  TpValueToMatchNum and scoring behaviour.

- new counter (includes terminating pods) is used only to seed
  CriticalPaths and compute the global minimum.

This prevents unreachable terminating zones from lowering the skew baseline
while preserving the rolling-update preference introduced in #87621.

Tests:
- Updated existing terminating-pod test semantics
- Added regression test for the 3-zone deadlock scenario (#116629)
- Strengthened integration

commit_message:
disable unnecessary Ubuntu services during node bootstrap

Mask and stop services that compete with apt operations or are not
needed for Kubernetes nodes:

- apt-news.service/timer: fetches APT news, holds apt lock
- esm-cache.service: Ubuntu Pro cache updates
- snapd.service/socket: Snap package manager
- lxd-installer.socket: LXD container helper
- ubuntu-advantage.service: Ubuntu Pro auto-attach
- unattended-upgrades.service: automatic security updates
- motd-news.timer: MOTD news fetching
- update-notifier-motd.timer: "new Ubuntu version" checks
- update-notifier-download.timer: failed package retry

This addresses CI timeouts where apt-news.service running concurrently
with apt-get update caused the master node to take ~5 minutes for
package index downloads (vs ~5-9 seconds on worker nodes).

Signed-off-by: Davanum Srinivas <davanum@gmail.com>

commit_message:
Move SAML metadata resolution to background thread (#150037)

OpenSAML has very coarse grained locking - for example
`AbstractInitializableComponent.isInitialized` is `synchronized`

That can lead to threads being blocked if they attempt to interact
with the `AbstractReloadingMetadataResolver`, particularly if it is
resolving metadata at the time (which may involve network calls).

This commit changes the `SamlRealm` to _never_ interact directly with
the OpenSAML resolver. Instead, a periodic (60s) task calls the
resolver and sets the resolved entity descriptor into a cached value
that the SamlRealm can use.

Resolves: #138031
Backport of: #144381

simplifies the API and keeps the oversampling logic centralized.

by passing the overSampleFactor parameter to all IVF KNN query variants,

fix: NPE on null zeroTermsQuery in cross_fields query (#149935)

* Guard against null zeroTermsQuery in cross_fields

#143220 added query.visit(queryVisitor) after the
zeroTermsQuery.asQuery() fallback to enforce the boolean
clause limit during query construction. asQuery() returns
null for ZeroTermsQueryOption.NONE, so the unconditional
visit() call throws NullPointerException whenever a token
in a cross_fields query_string analyzes to zero terms (for
example a stopword on a stopword-stripping analyzer).

The sibling MatchQueryParser was updated with a null guard
in the same PR; mirror it here. Adds a regression test that
exercises both the NONE and ALL branches of the fallback.

* Add changelog entry for #149935

* Guard against null zeroTermsQuery in cross_fields

#143220 added query.visit(queryVisitor) after the
zeroTermsQuery.asQuery() fallback to enforce the boolean
clause limit during query construction. asQuery() returns
null for ZeroTermsQueryOption.NONE, so the unconditional
visit() call throws NullPointerException whenever a token
in a cross_fields query_string analyzes to zero terms (for
example a stopword on a stopword-stripping analyzer).

exercises both the NONE and ALL branches of the fallback.

commit_message:
Hot-reload workload-identity client SSL

Previously, rotating the workload-identity issuer client's
certificate or key required a node restart.

Watch the files referenced by workload_identity.ssl.* via
ResourceWatcherService and rebuild the SSLContext on change.
A ReloadableSchemeIoSessionStrategy wrapper registered against
"https" on the HC connection manager lets reload swap the
SSLIOSessionStrategy in place rather than rebuilding the
CloseableHttpAsyncClient, so in-flight requests are not aborted.

Each handshake stamps the IOSession with a monotonic rotation
epoch; a RotationAwareReuseStrategy retires connections whose
stamp no longer matches the current epoch as their next response
completes, bounding drain to one request-response cycle per
connection regardless of load shape.

fix: NPE on null zeroTermsQuery in cross_fields query (#149935)

* Guard against null zeroTermsQuery in cross_fields

#143220 added query.visit(queryVisitor) after the
zeroTermsQuery.asQuery() fallback to enforce the boolean
clause limit during query construction. asQuery() returns
null for ZeroTermsQueryOption.NONE, so the unconditional
visit() call throws NullPointerException whenever a token
in a cross_fields query_string analyzes to zero terms (for
example a stopword on a stopword-stripping analyzer).

The sibling MatchQueryParser was updated with a null guard
in the same PR; mirror it here. Adds a regression test that
exercises both the NONE and ALL branches of the fallback.

* Add changelog entry for #149935

commit_message:
PromQL: store WITHOUT labels as strings, not Attributes

WITHOUT labels are filter keys for _timeseries output - they don't need
resolution to FieldAttribute. Store them as Set<String> in
AcrossSeriesAggregate.withoutLabels() instead of List<Attribute>.

This simplifies the design and fixes #149793 where UnresolvedAttributes
couldn't be resolved and were filtered out by dimensionAttributes().

Changes:
- AcrossSeriesAggregate: add withoutLabels field (Set<String>)
- UnresolvedPromqlFunction: add withoutLabels field
- Parser: pass strings for WITHOUT, attributes only for BY
- LabelSetSpec: use Set<String> for exclusions
- TimeSeriesWithout: add constructor for label names
- Remove Analyzer workaround for resolving groupings

Closes #149793

commit_message:
ESQL: MV_EXPAND for flattened

MV_EXPAND doesn't limit which fields it processes, but this adds some
tests for MV_EXPAND operating on a flattened field. It removes support
for flattened from MV_SORT because we don't believe the field is really
sortable. We use
```
| MV_EXPAND flattened
| SORT FIELD_EXTRACT(flattened, "sub")
```
instead.

commit_message:
Fix two func test failures caused by the new validateResourceChanges check

The new "was added but no corresponding upper bounds file was changed" check
runs before validatePrimaryIds, breaking two tests that expected errors from
those later checks.

For "highest id in an referable definition should exist in an upper bounds
file": adding an unrelated upper bound change (9.3) makes changedUpperBoundNames
non-empty, bypassing the "was added" guard and letting the "highest id" check
fire as intended.

For "new definition must use increment": the test uses id 8123050 which has
patch=50, so the "primary id must not be patch version" check fires first.
With increment=100, any value failing the alignment check also has a non-zero
patch, making the increment check unreachable without disabling the patch
check. Setting shouldValidatePrimaryIdNotPatch=false isolates the increment
alignment check.

Relax csvNoneOnMultiValueDataFailsColumnMismatch warning regex

CsvCompressedFormatSpecIT part-5 failed across every compression × storage
combination because the test's first warningRegex expected the parse-error
context to contain the literal fixture filename ("mv_sample.csv"). The
compressed read path identifies the chunk by an in-memory buffer URL
("mem://chunk-0") instead of the original storage URL, so the regex never
matched and the warning surfaced as "Unexpected warning". Drop the
filename-anchor and accept any non-empty path identifier; the substantive
"Row [N] error: CSV row has [5] columns but schema defines [3] columns"
assertion (which is what actually proves the silent-drift contract) is
unchanged.

  errors handled per policy (policy: skip_row); affected rows/fields
  are listed below

commit_message:
AGGS: Limit buckets of date_histogram on range

When you run _search's `date_histogram` agg on a `date_range` field it
collects each document into *each* range.

For example, if you had a range from `2000-01-01 to 3000-01-01` and did
a range of `1 year` it'd collect 3000 buckets. I you use a longer range
and a smaller bucket, well, you get far more buckets. Worse, if you use
a very *large* bucket size then you can trigger an overflow in the date
rounding and end up in the same buckets over and over again and be stuck
in an infinite loop.

As much as we'd love to prevent the overflow, we should guard against a
huge number of buckets. This does this by limiting the number of buckets
each document can live in to 10,000. That'll prevent circuit breaking
errors from small ranges. And it'll fail nicely on the overflow.

Delegate the choice of which region to evict to a dedicated EvictionPolicy. The LFU data structures are kept in the cache service and the order of iterating over candidates to evict is also not changed (from 0 to maxFreq).

In the future, we could change EvictionPolicy to return an iterator over the entries to attempt to evict. I kept this aside for now as it would require to make FreqLevel and LFUCacheEntry public and inject FreqLevel[] when instantiating the EvictionPolicy

commit_message:
[ESQL] DOC partitioning by default for COUNT

Follow-up to #149642, which made DOC partitioning safe for counts
but did not change the default routing. Under AUTO, COUNT queries
were still pinned to SEGMENT regardless of how many CPUs were
available, leaving most cores idle on counts that had to iterate
the index (e.g. URL LIKE "*google*").

LuceneCountOperator now picks DOC under AUTO for any non-trivial
query. A new LuceneSliceQueue.LeafSplitGuard lets the count
operator probe Weight.count(leaf) per leaf at plan time: leaves
where the shortcut returns a non-negative count are emitted as a
single full-leaf slice, so the O(1) shortcut still fires via
LuceneScorer.coversFullLeaf(); leaves where the shortcut returns
-1 fall through to the adaptive DOC partitioner. This way COUNT
gets per-leaf shortcut amortization where possible and per-leaf
sub-segment parallelism where iteration is required.

The DOC partitioner's slicing math is tightened so the slice
count and per-slice size hold up

Fix NumberFieldBlockLoaderTestCase for non-latin Unicode digits in ignored_source path (#150035)

When synthetic source is enabled with doc_values disabled,
the block loader reads from _ignored_source via
NumberFallbackSyntheticSourceReader, which uses the same
XContentParser-based parse path as indexing and accepts
non-latin Unicode digits. The previous fix (#149438)
distinguished only doc_values from stored_source, missing
this third path.

Introduces a ValueSource enum (DOC_VALUES, IGNORED_SOURCE,
STORED_SOURCE) to route coercion correctly, adds a
regression test, and improves the Javadoc.

It also fixes swallowing `CircuitBreakingException` in broad `catch (Exception e)` blocks.

commit_message:
fix: restore array parsing for `req.query` repeated keys (#7147)

qs 6.14 enforces a default `arrayLimit` of 20, which caused the
extended query parser to collapse query strings with more than 20
repeated values (e.g. `?ids=1&ids=2&...&ids=25`) into an object
instead of an array. This regressed in 4.22.0 (with the bump to
`qs@~6.14.1`) and broke existing consumers relying on the pre-6.14
behavior.

Pass `arrayLimit: Infinity` to `qs.parse` in
`parseExtendedQueryString` so repeated keys always produce arrays,
matching the behavior of Express \<= 4.21.x. Added a regression test
in `test/req.query.js` that sends 25 repeated values and asserts
they round-trip as an array.

fix: handle unknown Content-Type in res.set() falling back to original value

When mime.contentType() returns false for unrecognized types,
res.set('Content-Type', value) was setting the header to the
literal string 'false'. This change falls back to the original
value, matching how res.type() already handles this case.

Fixes: #7034

commit_message:
fix(redirect): throw TypeError instead of deprecating on missing/invalid url

Fixes #6941

Instead of sending a malformed Location header with 'undefined' or deprecated values, res.redirect() now throws a TypeError immediately when called without a valid url argument or with invalid argument types.

This is a breaking change for v6.x as indicated by the 'deprecate' label on the issue.

BREAKING CHANGE: res.redirect() now throws TypeError instead of deprecating:
- res.redirect() with no arguments
- res.redirect(undefined)
- res.redirect(url) where url is not a string
- res.redirect(status) where status is not a number

REF: make TimedeltaArray.total_seconds match the scalar at all magnitudes

The vectorized path computed asi8 / pps, which rounds at the nanosecond
magnitude and so disagreed with Timedelta.total_seconds by 1 ulp for ns
values above 2**53 (only the integer-second boundary case matched).
Mirror the scalar's `int_seconds + sub_ns / 1e9` split via divmod so the
results are identical at every magnitude, and gate the nextafter boundary
nudge on |asi8| > 2**53, the only regime where the collapse can occur
(GH#46819).

Also drop a duplicate whatsnew entry that misattributed the fix to the
closed GH#31043 (dateutil DST), and note the index/Series.dt variants in
the notable-bug-fixes section.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

arrays (platform int, i.e. int32 on 32-bit) against an expected built
from Python int lists (always int64), which mismatched on Linux-32-bit
and Pyodide. Pin the input arrays to int64 so the result dtype is
int64 on every platform.

BUG: DataFrame(list_of_arrays) with ragged same-dtype rows

The uniform-dtype fast path added in GH-64958 derived the column count
from the first row only (ncols = len(data[0])) and indexed every row by
that width. A longer first row raised IndexError; a shorter first row
silently dropped trailing values. Gate the fast path on uniform row
lengths so ragged rows fall through to the object/pad path and are
padded to max width with NaN, matching list-of-lists behavior.

Fix CI: use non-deprecated _inferred_freq_str in dt64arr_to_periodarr

The Series.dt.freq deprecation forced the internal caller in
dt64arr_to_periodarr off data.dt.freq, but it landed on
data._values.inferred_freq, which is itself deprecated (GH#64679).
That tripped the Pandas4Warning under -W error in CI. Use the
non-deprecated internal _inferred_freq_str instead, which returns the
identical value the original data.dt.freq did.

commit_message:
Don't unconditionally wrap generation_config.eos_token_id in align_special_tokens

When the tokenizer's EOS already matches what's in the model config and
generation config, align_special_tokens still converted the scalar
eos_token_id into a list as a side effect of the membership check it used
to detect new EOS tokens. That broke Whisper long-form generation: after
Trainer.train() called align_special_tokens, generate() compared
seek_sequence[-1] == generation_config.eos_token_id, which silently became
scalar == list (always False), and on silence the sequence ended up empty
because the pad-stripping branch no longer recognised pad == eos. The
result was an IndexError out of generation_whisper.py.

Move the int -> list conversion inside the branch that actually adds a new
EOS, and handle both shapes when merging. No behaviour change when the
tokenizer brings a new EOS token; the only difference is that the scalar
form is preserved when nothing needs aligning.

Fixes #45584

commit_message:
Fix StopIteration crash in get_text_with_replacements for unmatched multimodal tokens

- Handle multimodal tokens in text that have no corresponding
  replacement data (e.g. <|video|> with videos=None)
- Use next(iter, None) sentinel instead of bare next() to avoid
  StopIteration when the replacement iterator is exhausted
- Preserve the original token text in the output when no replacement
  is available, matching pre-#45493 behavior
- Regression introduced in ba06e3fbdf (#45493) which refactored
  ProcessorMixin.__call__ into get_text_with_replacements with
  strict iterator consumption over all regex-matched tokens
- Reproduces when downstream frameworks (e.g. vLLM) send profiling
  prompts containing multimodal placeholder tokens without actual
  multimodal data attached
)

Signed-off-by: Luciano Martins <lucianommartins@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Fix TAPAS tokenizer crash on pandas 3.x string-dtype tables (#45916)

* Fix TAPAS tokenizer crash on pandas 3.x string-dtype tables

`add_numeric_table_values` overwrites every cell of the input DataFrame
with a `Cell` dataclass instance. In pandas 3.x, string columns default
to the pyarrow-backed `StringDtype`, whose `_maybe_convert_setitem_value`
calls `len()` on the assignee to distinguish scalars from sequences. The
`Cell` dataclass has no `__len__`, so the write raises `TypeError`,
crashing `table-question-answering` pipelines on pandas 3.x.

Cast the (already-copied) table to `object` dtype before the loop so
arbitrary Python objects are accepted again. Behavior on pandas 2.x is
unchanged. Fixes #45901.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix the behaviour and add a proper end-to-end test

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cp): regenerate modeling_qwen3_omni_moe.py for inherited _cp_plan

Qwen3OmniMoeTalkerForConditionalGeneration inherits from
Qwen3MoeForCausalLM, so adding _cp_plan to the Qwen3-MoE modular source
in the previous commit cascades a +1 line into the regenerated
modeling_qwen3_omni_moe.py. The talker uses the same model.layers.*.self_attn
qualified-name shape (self.model = Qwen3OmniMoeTalkerModel(...)), so
the inherited plan applies without override.

Caught by CircleCI check_modular_conversion.

commit_message:
Fix TAPAS tokenizer crash on pandas 3.x string-dtype tables (#45916)

* Fix TAPAS tokenizer crash on pandas 3.x string-dtype tables

`add_numeric_table_values` overwrites every cell of the input DataFrame
with a `Cell` dataclass instance. In pandas 3.x, string columns default
to the pyarrow-backed `StringDtype`, whose `_maybe_convert_setitem_value`
calls `len()` on the assignee to distinguish scalars from sequences. The
`Cell` dataclass has no `__len__`, so the write raises `TypeError`,
crashing `table-question-answering` pipelines on pandas 3.x.

Cast the (already-copied) table to `object` dtype before the loop so
arbitrary Python objects are accepted again. Behavior on pandas 2.x is
unchanged. Fixes #45901.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix the behaviour and add a proper end-to-end test

fix(cp): mirror TP's initialize_/distribute_ split + gate tp_plan="auto"

Two related fixes on the CP integration:

1. Gate the legacy `tp_plan = "auto"` shortcut on
   `distributed_config.enable_expert_parallel`. The previous condition
   `if distributed_config is not None and tp_plan is None: tp_plan = "auto"`
   fired for ANY `DistributedConfig`, including the CP-only case. That
   activated the TP path which then refuses to run alongside the
   `device_map` users naturally pass for the per-rank model placement
   CP needs ("`tp_plan` and `device_map` are mutually exclusive").
   With the new gate, a CP-only `DistributedConfig` no longer attaches
   the TP runtime — only an EP-flagged one does. This was reproduced on
   the real `openai/gpt-oss-20b` and turned `MODE=cp` `torchrun` runs
   from a crash into the headline +85/+105/+128 % tok/s numbers.

   matches `initialize_tensor_parallelism` / `distribute_model`:

* `modeling_flash_attention_utils._flash_attention_forward`: the "no padding"
  branch unconditionally called `flash_fn`, which is `None` for varlen-only
  kernels (the metal kernel only ships `flash_attn_varlen_func`). Synthesize
  `cu_seqlens` for the dense batched layout and route through `flash_varlen_fn`
  in that case. `.contiguous()` before reshape is required: the cached
  K/V (post-transpose) is non-contiguous and the Metal kernel reads garbage
  off it during decode, producing nonsense tokens.

* `continuous_batching/requests.get_device_and_memory_breakdown`: on MPS,
  `torch.mps.driver_allocated_memory()` returns bytes currently held by the
  Metal driver (≈0 right after process start), not the total.

chore(deps): bump postgres-bytea to 1.0.1 to drop Buffer() deprecation (#29538)

## Problem

Reading a `Bytes` column through `@prisma/adapter-neon`,
`@prisma/adapter-pg`, or `@prisma/adapter-ppg` emits Node.js `DEP0005`
because `pg-types`' `BYTEA` parser is
[`postgres-bytea@1.0.0`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/postgres-bytea/v/1.0.0),
which still uses the deprecated `new Buffer(...)` constructor.

## Fix


[`postgres-bytea@1.0.1`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/postgres-bytea/v/1.0.1)
(released 2025-12-17) swaps `new Buffer(...)` for `Buffer.from ||
Buffer` and stays inside the `~1.0.0` range that `pg-types` declares, so
a lockfile refresh is enough — no `package.json` or source changes are
required.

This commit updates the three `pnpm-lock.yaml` references (resolution
block, snapshot block, and the single consumer entry under
`pg-types@2.x`) from `1.0.0` to `1.0.1`. `pnpm install --lockfile-only
--frozen-lockfile` round-trips cleanly.

commit_message:
Harden ~/.config/prisma-platform/auth.json file permissions to 0o600

CredentialsStore.writeCredentialsToDisk writes the Prisma Platform OAuth
tokens (token + refreshToken per workspaceId) to the auth file via
writeFile(this.authFilePath, JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)) with no mode
option. Node's default 0o666 masked by umask 022 gives 0o644 on macOS
Terminal and most Linux defaults, so the file ends up world-readable.
The surrounding directory was likewise being created at 0o755 via
mkdir(... { recursive: true }) with no mode.

Any local account or process that can traverse the home directory can
recover the token + refreshToken and call the Prisma Platform management
API as the user.

This commit:
- Adds `chmod` to the fs/promises imports.
- Passes `{ mode: 0o600 }` to writeFile and `{ mode: 0o700 }` to mkdir.
- Adds a follow-up chmod for both file and directory so pre-existing
  installs converge to 0o600/0o700 on the next save. Per Node docs,
  fs.chmod on Windows silently no-ops b

chore(deps): bump postgres-bytea to 1.0.1 to drop Buffer() deprecation (#29538)

## Problem

Reading a `Bytes` column through `@prisma/adapter-neon`,
`@prisma/adapter-pg`, or `@prisma/adapter-ppg` emits Node.js `DEP0005`
because `pg-types`' `BYTEA` parser is
[`postgres-bytea@1.0.0`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/postgres-bytea/v/1.0.0),
which still uses the deprecated `new Buffer(...)` constructor.

## Fix


[`postgres-bytea@1.0.1`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/postgres-bytea/v/1.0.1)
(released 2025-12-17) swaps `new Buffer(...)` for `Buffer.from ||
Buffer` and stays inside the `~1.0.0` range that `pg-types` declares, so
a lockfile refresh is enough — no `package.json` or source changes are
required.

This commit updates the three `pnpm-lock.yaml` references (resolution
block, snapshot block, and the single consumer entry under
`pg-types@2.x`) from `1.0.0` to `1.0.1`. `pnpm install --lockfile-only
--frozen-lockfile` round-trips cleanly.

commit_message:
chore: disable scheduled CI; run on push/PR/manual dispatch

ORM iteration has slowed enough that the nightly test matrix and the
half-hourly BuildPulse analytics upload are no longer worth the CI spend.
Both lose their `schedule:` triggers; `workflow_dispatch:` is preserved
so they remain manually runnable. The `schedule:` blocks are commented
out (not deleted) so re-enabling is a one-PR uncomment when ORM
iteration resumes. `test.yml` itself is untouched — push/PR-triggered
CI keeps running on `main`.

The README's `Ecosystem Tests Status` badge is also removed: it points
at a workflow on a different repo whose schedule is being disabled in
the same coordinated effort, and once that schedule is off, the badge
would freeze at whatever colour it had on disable day. Risks
broadcasting a stale-red signal indefinitely. The `Prisma Tests Status`
badge stays — it's driven by push, not cron, and won't rot.

fix(bootstrap): add scripted mode, reorder deps, capture subprocess errors

Three changes to make `prisma bootstrap` work reliably in non-interactive
environments (AI agents, CI) and improve diagnostics:

1. Scripted mode: when both `--api-key` and `--database` are provided,
   all `confirm()` prompts are auto-accepted. In an empty directory,
   defaults to the `nextjs` template. This removes the TTY requirement
   that caused hangs in Claude Code / Cursor agents.

2. Deps-before-link: the dependency gate (dotenv, prisma, @prisma/client)
   now runs before the link step. Previously, if link failed after init
   but before deps were installed, re-running `prisma bootstrap` crashed
   with "Cannot find module 'dotenv/config'" at config load time.

3. Subprocess stderr capture: `runLocalPrismaCommand` now uses `spawn`
   with a piped stderr stream instead of `execFileSync` with inherited
   stdio. This captures stderr for telemetry while still displaying it
   to the user, and propagates

rethrew the raw `DriverAdapterError` unchanged.

column whose unique index was dropped in the DB raises Postgres 42P10

specification"), which is not individually mapped by the adapter. These
errors are not bugs and end users need to see the underlying DB code and

commit_message:
refactor(adapter-libsql): address review feedback on socket error handling

- Replace single-level isSocketError / mapSocketError with a cause-chain
  traversal via findSocketError so deeply nested wrapping (e.g. AggregateError
  or future @libsql/client changes) is handled defensively
- Remove redundant 'as string' cast in isRawSocketError; the preceding typeof
  guard is sufficient
- Add address/port/hostname to socket error test fixtures and assert the
  DatabaseNotReachable host/port mapping contract explicitly
- Same fix for HRANA_WEBSOCKET_ERROR wrapped-error test cases
- Tighten the re-throw test to verify the original object is preserved

fix(adapter-mssql): handle socket errors that bypass isDriverError

Socket errors (ENOTFOUND, ECONNREFUSED, ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT) from the
mssql driver lack the numeric `error.number` field required by
isDriverError, so they fell through to `throw error` unwrapped rather
than being returned as typed MappedError values (DatabaseNotReachable,
ConnectionClosed, SocketTimeout).

Added isSocketError guard checked before isDriverError, matching the
pattern used in adapter-pg, adapter-neon, and adapter-libsql.

Also adds errors.test.ts covering the major error code mappings and all
four socket error codes.

commit_message:
fix(adapter-libsql): handle socket errors before isDriverError check

Socket errors (ENOTFOUND, ECONNREFUSED, ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT) satisfy
the LibsqlError type guard — they have a string `code`, string `message`,
and undefined `rawCode` — so they slipped through `isDriverError` and
were returned as `{ kind: 'sqlite', extendedCode: 1 }` instead of the
correct `DatabaseNotReachable`, `ConnectionClosed`, or `SocketTimeout`.

The fix mirrors the pattern used in adapter-pg and adapter-neon: check
`isSocketError` before `isDriverError` to short-circuit before the
SQLite dispatch table.

fix(adapter-neon): correct TIMESTAMPTZ conversion, add UTC suffix to writes, add TIMETZ_ARRAY mapping

Three related bugs affected TIMESTAMPTZ and TIMETZ columns/arrays in
adapter-neon when the PostgreSQL server runs in a non-UTC timezone.

**Bug 1 — normalize_timestamptz (reads)**
`normalize_timestamptz` swapped the offset label to '+00:00' without
converting the actual time. For a server in UTC-6, a stored UTC instant
is returned as '09:26:34-06' but was emitted as '09:26:34+00:00' instead
of the correct '15:26:34+00:00', silently corrupting every TIMESTAMPTZ
read. The fix parses the string through Date to perform the actual UTC
conversion, preserving microsecond precision that JavaScript Date drops.

**Bug 2 — formatDateTime (writes)**
`formatDateTime` produced timestamps without a timezone offset
(e.g. '2025-11-24 09:26:34.887'). PostgreSQL treats an offset-free
TIMESTAMPTZ value as session-local time, so on a non-UTC server the
wrong instant was stored. Adding '+00:00' tells Postg

commit_message:
fix(adapter-neon): use error.column for NullConstraintViolation and fix ColumnNotFound for unquoted names

PostgreSQL NOT NULL violations (23502) populate `error.column` with the
violating column name. The `error.detail` field contains
"Failing row contains (...)" — not the "Key (...)" format used by
unique-violation (23505) — so the regex that was used never matched,
causing `meta.target` to always be empty ([]) for P2011 errors.

Fix by reading `error.column` directly, consistent with adapter-pg.

For ColumnNotFound (42703), the old implementation
(`error.message.split(' ').at(1)?.split('"').at(1)`) only handled
quoted column names. The improved regex
(`/^column (.+) does not exist$/`) handles unquoted names, qualified
names, and escaped quotes, matching what adapter-pg already does since
#29307.

Adds an errors.test.ts covering all cases for both error codes.

commit_message:
fix(adapter-pg): use error.column for NullConstraintViolation constraint field

PostgreSQL's 23502 (NOT NULL violation) error sets `error.column` directly to the
violating column name. The previous implementation applied the regex
`/Key \(([^)]+)\)/` to `error.detail`, which is the unique-violation (23505) format.
For NOT NULL errors, `detail` contains "Failing row contains (...)" which never
matches that pattern, so `constraint` was always `undefined` and `meta.target` was
never populated for P2011 errors.

Fix: read `error.column` instead of parsing `error.detail`.

Updated the existing test to use real PostgreSQL error data (detail = "Failing row
contains ...", column = "foo") and added a second test for the case where
`error.column` is absent.

Fixes: https://github.com/prisma/prisma/issues (P2011 meta.target always empty)

commit_message:
refactor(adapter-pg): simplify mutex to runExclusive per CodeRabbit

Replace the manual acquire/try/finally/release pattern in
PgTransaction.performIO with async-mutex's built-in `runExclusive`, which
handles acquire and release internally.  Semantically identical to the
previous implementation — serialises all performIO calls on the underlying
pg.PoolClient — but removes boilerplate and avoids any risk of a missed
release on unexpected throws.

Addresses CodeRabbit suggestion on PR #29468.

commit_message:
fix(client-engine-runtime): populate meta.target for P2002 and P2011 errors

The Rust query engine populates `meta.target` on P2002 (UniqueConstraintViolation)
and P2011 (NullConstraintViolation) errors so that callers can identify which
field(s) caused the constraint violation. The JS driver-adapter runtime path was
throwing those errors with `meta` containing only `driverAdapterError`, leaving
`meta.target` always undefined.

`extractMeta` now reads the structured constraint information already present in
the DriverAdapterError and maps it to the standard `meta.target` field:
- When the adapter resolved field names (e.g. adapter-pg parses the PG error
  detail), `target` is set to that `string[]`.
- When the adapter only has an index name (e.g. adapter-mariadb, adapter-mssql),
  `target` is set to `[indexName]` so callers always get a consistent type.

The existing `driverAdapterError` meta key is preserved for backward compatibility.

Fixes #29344

commit_message:
fix(adapters): serialize JSON args with Decimal-aware replacer

`Decimal.prototype.toJSON` returns the string representation of the value,
so `JSON.stringify({ n: new Decimal("42") })` produces `{"n":"42"}` (a JSON
string) rather than the expected `{"n":42}` (a JSON number).

Each driver adapter's `mapArg` now pre-serialises JSON arguments using a
custom replacer that converts Decimal-like instances (detected by constructor
name and the presence of `toNumber`) to their numeric value before the
underlying driver library gets a chance to call `JSON.stringify` itself.

Also adds the missing `'JSON'` decltype case in adapter-libsql so that
columns declared as `JSON` are mapped to `ColumnTypeEnum.Json` (only `JSONB`
was handled before).

Fixes #29387

commit_message:
fix(client-engine-runtime): serialize join children inside transactions

When `update` (or any write) with `include` relations is executed inside a
transaction, the `join` node in the query interpreter fires a `Promise.all`
over all child relation fetches. Each child eventually calls `queryRaw` on
`context.queryable`, which — inside a transaction — is a single `pg.PoolClient`
(not a pool). Concurrent `client.query()` calls on a single pg Client trigger:

  "Calling client.query() when the client is already executing a query is
  deprecated and will be removed in pg@9.0."

This becomes a hard error in pg@9.0.

Fix: detect whether `context.queryable` is a `Transaction` (via the `commit`
property on the `Transaction` interface) and, if so, fetch the join children
sequentially instead of in parallel. When using a connection pool the existing
parallel behaviour is preserved.

Fixes #29407

## Summary

Addresses product testing feedback
([PTL-1372](https://linear.app/prisma-company/issue/PTL-1372)) for
`prisma bootstrap`:

- **Template download timeout** — increased from 30s to 120s. Added
proper error handling on `nodeStream` in `decompressGzip` to prevent
unhandled `DOMException` crashes on Node 25. Timeout errors now show a
user-friendly message.
- **Auto-install missing deps** — instead of dead-ending with "install
manually and re-run", the command now prompts to install missing
`dotenv`/`prisma` via the detected package manager (`npm`, `pnpm`,
`yarn`, `bun`).
- **Resumable re-run** — when `--database` is passed on an
already-linked project, bootstrap now skips the link step and continues
to migrate/generate/seed instead of blocking with "already linked, use
--force".
- **Partial deps accuracy** — only lists actually missing dependencies
in the prompt, not all checked

fn providers that implement the dispatch surface declared (later in
this phase) in turbo-tasks/src/handle.rs.

    providers).
  - test : pulls in turbo-tasks-testing (will emit __tt_test_*
    providers).

Building with neither feature compiles to an empty lib, so 'cargo
check --workspace' works without flags. Binaries and tests that
actually consume the dispatch must enable the appropriate feature(s).

Fix `'use cache'` bail-out under `unstable_instant = false` (#94198)

This fixes a bug where pages exporting `unstable_instant = false` cause
their `'use cache'` reads to be incorrectly treated as dynamic, so the
build emits an empty static shell where it should contain the cached
content.

The root cause sits in the cache wrapper's Resume Data Cache (RDC) miss
bail-out. When prerendering a fallback shell whose RDC is the prefilled,
read-only seed from a phase-1 prerender of a more-specific sibling
route, a `'use cache'` miss is short-circuited to a dynamic hole — under
that contract a miss means the cache key depends on a fallback param.
That bail was gated on `workUnitStore.allowEmptyStaticShell`, which
originally coincided with "we have a read-only seed" because the
fallback-shell flow was the only thing setting the flag. #89077 widened
the flag to also cover `unstable_instant = false`, which has no seed, so
the bail started firing for routes that should be allowed to fill their
cac

commit_message:
perf: use createElement instead of createElementNS for HTML elements (#18262)

## Summary

The current wrapper always calls `document.createElementNS(namespace ??
NAMESPACE_HTML, tag, options)` — even for HTML elements (the >99% case),
and even when `options` would be `undefined`. Two effects compound:

1. **Route HTML elements through `createElement`** — Blink has a fast
path that skips the namespace lookup `createElementNS` always performs.
2. **Omit the trailing `undefined` argument** — V8/Blink take a slower
path for `createElementNS(ns, tag, undefined)` (and `createElement(tag,
undefined)`) than for the bare 2-arg form. This applies symmetrically to
the SVG/MathML branch, where the wrapper now also avoids the `undefined`
3rd arg.

The wrapper dispatches to the fastest call shape for every input —
`{HTML, non-HTML}` × `{with is, without is}` × no `undefined` ever.

## Affects

Every place Svelte constructs a DOM element internally:
`<svelte:element>`, `run_scripts`, the per-compone

docs: add auto-generated browser support page (#18276)

## Summary

Adds a [Browser
support](https://github.com/MathiasWP/svelte/blob/document-pipeline-draft/documentation/docs/07-misc/05-browser-support.md)
page listing the minimum browser versions Svelte's runtime and compiler
output require. The page (headline floor + per-feature requirements) is
auto-generated by `packages/svelte/scripts/generate-browser-support.js`,
which scans the code Svelte actually ships against the
[web-features](https://github.com/web-platform-dx/web-features) Baseline
dataset and resolves results to concrete browser versions via
[baseline-browser-mapping](https://github.com/web-platform-dx/baseline-browser-mapping).
CI fails if a PR moves the floor without regenerating the page.

For 5.55.9 the floor is **Baseline 2020**: Chrome/Edge 87, Firefox 83,
Safari 14.

## How it works

1. **Headline floor.** Each runtime entry from `pkg.exports` is bundled
with rollup using production conditions, then walked with T

chore: replace custom renderer type arguments with a single one (#18244)

Alternative to #18216

Allows for inference to still works but also allow for explicit
declaration in the cases where it's needed.

I made some changes to the code proposed by @mrkishi (I used `unique
symbol` for the `DefaultType`, inferred the `NodeType`) but overall is
mostly his work.

I've also replaced the renderer for the test with a `TS` version of it
so we can better test the types there.

I think this is the best middle ground solution...inference works (when
it works...we can document that you need to put the create methods first
and the gotchas of automatic inference) but people can also quickly
specify their types in an object.

perf: store current_sources as Set for O(1) membership checks (#18278)

`current_sources` tracks the sources created within the active reaction
so that reading or writing them during that same reaction doesn't
trigger a re-run. It was an `Array` checked with

fix: prevent batch unlinking twice (#18303)

Merged #18298 a bit too soon - there's still a situation which can
corrput the linked list: If we merge one batch into another, it will
unlink the batch immediately. But `discard` also calls it, running the
unlink logic again, which can corrupt the linked list.

Sketch:

1. Batch A is pending.
2. Batch B starts later, intersects A, resolves first, and merges into
A.
3. B is unlinked immediately, but `A.oncommit(() => B.discard())`
remains.
4. Independent batch C is created while A is still pending and is linked
after A.
5. A commits, calls `B.discard()`, and B's stale `#prev`/`#next` can set
`A.#next = null` / `last_batch = A`, disconnecting C.

Not able to produce a failing test from it but it's definitely a fix we
need to make.

Also moved `#link` into a constructor, because it is (and should be)
used only once.

Also made the action after an error `discard` instead of just `#unlink`
because this batch is done for and e.g. pending `settled

fix: reject pending async deriveds on discard

The rejects all async deriveds of a batch as `OBSOLETE`, so they don't hang around and bail early without triggering the batch.

If we don't do this, an async derived can trigger the already done batch, which schedules an effect that is never flushed. Because it is never flushed the branches it touched on its way up are never cleared, and so anything else in that subtree is now unreactive.

perf: use Set instead of Array for constant lookups in utils.js (#18250)

Several constant lookup tables in `utils.js` were arrays searched with
`Array.prototype.includes`, which is O(n). They're queried often — per
attribute during attribute setup and SSR, per event during event
delegation, and per identifier during compilation. Switching them to
`Set` makes each lookup O(1) without changing any public behaviour.

feat: derive tested subpackage exports from package.json

Replaces the hand-curated CONST that listed which subpackages and which
of their exports to test with dynamic enumeration. The pipeline now:

1. Walks every entry in pkg.exports
2. Skips a small SKIP_SUBPACKAGES set (the main entry, server-only,
   internal, and types-only entries — each justified in the comment)
3. Dynamically imports each remaining subpath with `import * as ns`
4. Generates a fixture for every named export

71 exports across 9 subpackages are now discovered automatically
(previously 30 across 5). New subpackages and new exports get picked
up on the next run with no script edit.

The 41 extra fixtures (mostly easing functions and svelte/store
exports) all pass at the runtime floor — the conditional table is
unchanged.

feat: auto-validate conditional features against source

Replaces the hand-edited "Per-feature browser requirements" markdown
table with structured data (CONDITIONAL_FEATURES) that drives both the
rendered table and a per-entry validator. Adds drift detection
(CONDITIONAL_SOURCE_FILES) that scans every conditionally-loaded source
file and fails the build if it flags a browser API that is not
documented in CONDITIONAL_FEATURES or justified in IGNORE_FEATURES.

Per-entry validation (option C):
- For each entry with `detection: { feature_id, baseline_year }`, the
  scanner lints the named files at year `baseline_year - 1` and
  verifies `feature_id` is flagged. Catches stale entries where the
  API was removed or renamed.
- Entries with `detection: 'manual'` (string-literal options, .zoom
  reads, etc.) only check file existence.

Drift detection (option B):
- Per-file scan over CONDITIONAL_SOURCE_FILES at the runtime floor.
- Any flagged feature not in `documented_ids` causes the build t

cleanup: collapse array+set declarations into single Sets

Addresses review feedback from @dummdidumm:

- No more "array first, corresponding set second" duplication. Each group
  is now declared as `new Set(/** @type {const} */ ([...]))` — the inner

  inferred at the type level.

- The `typeof X[number]` cast is replaced with
  `typeof X extends Set<infer T> ? T : never`, so the `RuneName` /
  `StateCreationRuneName` / `RawTextElement` typedefs still auto-derive
  from the Set's contents (no manual literal duplication).

fix: remove raw-text hydration markers (#18269)

Fixes #14413.

This keeps the temporary raw-text hydration sentinel used by dynamic
`<svelte:element>` from becoming part of the final DOM. Hydration still
gets a marker to advance through for raw-text children, but the marker
is removed after the child renderer runs, so `<style>` and `<script>`
contents stay identical to SSR output.

Tests:
- `pnpm test hydration -t svelte-head-dynamic-style`
- `pnpm test hydration`
- `pnpm test runtime-runes -t svelte-element`
- `pnpm lint`
- `git diff --check`

perf: walk composedPath() directly in delegated event propagation (#18268)

## Summary

The propagation walk in `handle_event_propagation` already calls
`event.composedPath()` at the start to find the entry index, but then
re-derives the same chain step-by-step via `current_target.assignedSlot
|| current_target.parentNode || .host`. Three property reads per
iteration is measurable on the hot event path.

Walk the captured `path` array by index instead.

## Notes on behavior

`composedPath()` is the spec-compliant snapshot of the dispatch chain:
- Same shadow-DOM crossings (slots and shadow roots are included for
composed events).
- Same `host` traversal (composed-path crosses shadow boundaries when
appropriate).
- Differs from the previous walk in one edge case: if a handler removes
a parent mid-dispatch, the snapshot-based walk continues through the
captured chain (matches native browser semantics — the previous
`parentNode` walk would have stopped at a null parent).

## Performance

fix: catch rejected promises while merging/committing (#18266)

A committing/merging batch can have promises that were rejected (e.g. as
obsolete). We gotta "forward" this rejection, too, instead of just the
successful promise. At best it results in a uncaught rejection
(`async-branch-merge-obsolete`), at worst it means error boundaries are
not correctly displayed (`async-later-promise-fails-first`).

Solves the reproduction in
https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/18221#issuecomment-4507803845

fix: unlink errored and otherwise finished batch (#18264)

This fixes the issue in
https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/18221#issuecomment-4497918414
where an error can create follup-up invariant errors. The batch errors,
has no chance to run otherwise (no more pending work) and is therefore
"dead". That means we need to unlink it otherwise it's becoming a
"zombie" and hangs around, causing unnecessary and potentially buggy (as
seen in the reproduction) merge/commit work.

I was not able to reduce the reproduction down to a test case that fails
without the fix, but it does make a related error test from #17888 work
more correctly.

fix: make unnecessary commit work less likely (#18263)

While looking at
https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/18221#issuecomment-4497918414
and trying to understand how the invariant can happen I noticed that we
are not correctly filtering during commit.
- we were not ignoring deriveds
- we were not comparing the correct values (checking `source.v` instead
of the saved value) and not checking if their "is a derived" state
differs

I'm not able to come up with a test where something fails without these
(possibly because it's more about an optimization to do less reruns and
not about correctness) fixes, but they do make sense.

commit_message:
fix: correctly coordinate component-level effects inside async blocks (#18260)

While looking at the reproduction in
https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/18221#issuecomment-4497918414
I immediately got greeted with a runtime error when running it in the
playground (weirdly not in the Stackblitz version). The error was that a
component expected a binding to be set in onMount, but the timing of
onMount was wrong.

Turns out it's because our logic to determine whether or not to defer
top level effects is flawed. `REACTION_RAN`, which was used previously,
is already set if the initialized component is inside an async block. We
instead check for `component_context.i` which is set to `true` on
`pop()`.
